Proposed Decision: The external catering provider is the authoritative source for menus, prices, allergens, station availability and food availability. SmartRail may cache/display this data but must not manually redefine it.
Your Reason: This creates a clear data-ownership and system boundary, keeps catering responsibility with the external provider, and fits the required external integration architecture
Notes / Open Questions: Menu cache refresh interval still needs definition.

Proposed Decision: For the MVP, the catering provider should own food-payment processing and remain merchant of record rather than SmartRail becoming the financial clearinghouse.
Your Reason: This gives payment responsibility to the system that already owns the food-ordering service. It keeps SmartRail focused on railway and journey coordination, avoids unnecessary payment/security/compliance complexity for the MVP, and maintains a clear boundary between SmartRail and the external catering provider.
Notes / Open Questions: Must align with refund and liability policy.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail may initiate the integrated ordering experience and display status, while the catering provider remains authoritative for order acceptance, payment result and commercial transaction state.
Your Reason: This provides passengers with a convenient integrated SmartRail experience without duplicating commercial order logic inside SmartRail. It keeps acceptance, payment, and transaction state with the catering provider that actually fulfils the order, while SmartRail focuses on journey integration and displaying the provider’s status.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact API contract remains to be designed.

Proposed Decision: Cancellation cut-off rules should be owned and finally enforced by the catering system. SmartRail may display rules and prevent obvious invalid actions, but the provider API is authoritative.
Your Reason: Cancellation affects the provider’s food preparation and commercial order state, so final enforcement should remain with the catering provider while SmartRail provides a convenient passenger experience.
Notes / Open Questions: Keeps catering business rules within the catering domain.

Proposed Decision: Item-level partial cancellation should be deferred from the MVP; food orders are cancelled as atomic orders.
Your Reason: Whole-order cancellation satisfies the core cancellation need while avoiding unnecessary order, refund, and integration complexity in the MVP.
Notes / Open Questions: Can be reconsidered post-MVP.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail should provide the best available ETA when reliable, but catering integration must also tolerate degraded information such as delay status or buffer windows when precise ETA is unavailable.
Your Reason: Catering should not depend entirely on a precise ETA(Estimated Time. Supporting degraded timing information keeps food coordination usable when live railway data is incomplete or unreliable.
Notes / Open Questions: Workshop disagreed over mandatory precise ETA versus simpler fallback.

Proposed Decision: Catering/order-quality issues should ultimately belong to the catering domain, while railway disruption and journey-information issues belong to SmartRail; SmartRail should route passengers to the correct support path.
Your Reason: This creates clear support ownership: catering handles food/order problems, while SmartRail handles railway problems, preventing responsibility from becoming unclear to passengers.
Notes / Open Questions: Missing/cold/incorrect-order first-contact workflow needs alignment with WS-002.

Proposed Decision: Railway-caused food-waste liability should be governed by a commercial SLA/policy between parties rather than automatically determined by SmartRail application logic.
Your Reason: Food-waste liability is a commercial agreement between the railway and catering provider, not a decision that SmartRail application logic should make automatically.
Notes / Open Questions: Proof-of-preparation and liability rules still require business clarification.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail/Customer Service should act as the passenger's primary support entry point instead of forcing passengers to determine which external vendor to contact.
Your Reason: A single SmartRail entry point gives passengers a simpler support experience while allowing issues to be routed internally to the responsible provider.
Notes / Open Questions: Internal escalation can still route the issue to catering.

Proposed Decision: Customer-service staff should not troubleshoot webhooks, API payloads, databases or message-reconciliation problems. Technical reconciliation must be handled automatically or by technical support.
Your Reason: This keeps responsibilities clear: customer service handles passenger issues, while automated mechanisms or technical staff handle system-level integration failures.
Notes / Open Questions: Keeps CSR responsibilities operational rather than technical.

Proposed Decision: Use an authoritative order-status API combined with idempotent asynchronous events/webhooks, with reconciliation after connectivity recovery.
Your Reason: Mandatory webhooks plus reconciliation may be excessive. Start with a reliable provider API, idempotent requests and status refresh; make webhooks optional.
Notes / Open Questions: Periodic reconciliation may act as fallback rather than primary real-time mechanism.

Proposed Decision: Refund execution should follow the merchant/payment owner defined for catering; SmartRail Customer Service may initiate or track a case without directly manipulating vendor financial records.
Your Reason: Retain provider payment responsibility, but don't imply SmartRail needs a refund case-tracking system.
Notes / Open Questions: Must remain consistent with AD-002.

Proposed Decision: Frontline staff should only provide predefined, bounded recovery actions such as approved vouchers/alternatives; larger financial recovery requires escalation.
Your Reason: Vouchers, financial recovery limits and frontline compensation approvals introduce a commercial workflow outside core MVP requirements.
Notes / Open Questions: Avoid unrestricted inventory or financial discretion.

Proposed Decision: The catering provider should own preparation stop/cancellation rules using SmartRail journey-status inputs rather than leaving the decision to Customer Service staff.
Your Reason: The catering provider controls food preparation, so it should apply its own stop/cancellation rules using journey updates from SmartRail rather than relying on Customer Service decisions.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact delay/cancellation thresholds require catering policy.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail should not automatically assign financial blame. Railway-side versus catering-side failure must be established through recorded events and an agreed fault-determination/SLA process.
Your Reason: SmartRail should record reliable evidence, not automatically assign financial blame. An agreed SLA process provides fair fault determination between SmartRail and the catering provider.
Notes / Open Questions: Workshop explicitly identified disputed financial fault ownership.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail should establish one authoritative operational journey-information source consumed by passenger apps, station systems and Customer Service.
Your Reason: A single authoritative journey source prevents conflicting information across passenger apps, stations, Customer Service, and integrations, keeping railway information consistent and trustworthy.
Notes / Open Questions: Prevents contradictory passenger information.

Proposed Decision: MVP should provide disruption rights/information, eligibility, journey context and guided handoffs rather than becoming a full financial/logistics fulfillment platform.
Your Reason: Formal passenger rights, eligibility evaluation and recovery handoffs are more complex than the disruption information required by the assessment.
Notes / Open Questions: Digital claim logging or structured handoff may still be supported.

Proposed Decision: Maintain an authoritative repository/feed of disruption-time inter-operator ticket-acceptance rules and publish those rules consistently to passengers and CSRs.
Your Reason: Multi-operator ticket acceptance is outside our ticketing-free MVP. No need to resolve its integration ownership now.
Notes / Open Questions: Ownership of updates from external operators must be defined.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail should communicate eligibility and handoff information for emergency accommodation or alternative transport but should not build an automated hotel-booking/taxi-dispatch engine for the MVP.
Your Reason: The MVP boundary is appropriate, but SmartRail should not determine eligibility itself; eligibility must come from approved railway/operator policy.
Notes / Open Questions: Handoff SLA remains unresolved.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail should preserve disruption/journey context and pre-populate reference details when handing passengers to an external recovery or claim process.
Your Reason: SmartRail should preserve disruption/journey context and securely pre-populate necessary, authorized reference details when handing passengers to an external recovery or claim process.
Notes / Open Questions: Avoids passengers repeatedly entering known journey information.

Proposed Decision: Use predefined operational/SLA thresholds with Central Control authority and local station input rather than leaving replacement-transport activation to ad-hoc individual discretion.
Your Reason: Transport activation thresholds and replacement-service decisions don't need implementing in SmartRail's MVP.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact threshold values remain business/operations policy.

Proposed Decision: Facility faults and replacement-transport information should originate from one authoritative state and propagate concurrently across station, Control, Customer Service and passenger channels.
Your Reason: Keep consistent incident and journey updates, but remove implied replacement-transport management and detailed facility-state workflows.
Notes / Open Questions: Local safety-critical alerts can still receive immediate priority.

Proposed Decision: During crises, assistance logging should be minimal/frictionless—such as one-tap or short-form capture—with fuller information completed later if required.
Your Reason: Separate passenger-assistance logging conflicts with our decision to avoid individual assistance-tracking workflows.
Notes / Open Questions: Avoid complex data entry during emergencies.

Proposed Decision: Physical escort/custody of vulnerable passengers should belong to designated station/assistance operational staff; Customer Service coordinates information rather than physical handling.
Your Reason: Physical passenger assistance requires trained on-site staff, while Customer Service should coordinate information rather than perform physical handling.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact organizational role may vary by station.

Proposed Decision: The host station/facility operator should own the operational status of lifts, ramps and related station accessibility assets, with SmartRail distributing that state to other channels.
Your Reason: We can define responsibility for maintaining basic verified station-accessibility information without building live asset management.
Notes / Open Questions: Multi-operator station governance needs confirmation.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail should support assistance coordination/status tracking but should avoid turning the workflow into a heavy multi-operator administrative system for the MVP.
Your Reason: Individual assistance tracking is not practical for the expected passenger volume and would add unnecessary MVP complexity.
Notes / Open Questions: Keep emergency interaction lightweight.

Proposed Decision: A defined low-tech/analog fallback must exist for vulnerability and accessibility assistance when digital connectivity is unavailable, followed by later reconciliation.
Your Reason: The fallback should stay within the SmartRail application ecosystem by supporting basic offline actions and later synchronization during connectivity loss.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact analog procedure remains unresolved.

Proposed Decision: Drivers must never become system administrators or troubleshoot servers/software during active operations. SmartRail must present clear operational degraded states and procedures.
Your Reason: Drivers should focus on safe train operations, while SmartRail handles technical failures through clear application warnings and approved operational procedures.
Notes / Open Questions: Strong workshop agreement.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail itself should not invent train-driving authority during total DMI failure. It should enter a critical degraded state, alert Control and direct users into the approved railway rulebook/manual fallback procedure.
Your Reason: A SmartRail driver app failure must not be confused with failure of a safety-critical train-driving interface.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact safe-driving procedure requires railway operational authority.

Proposed Decision: Cached operational data must have explicit validity/time limits. Expiry should trigger a defined degraded-state escalation rather than allowing indefinite stale-data use.
Your Reason: Outdated operational information could mislead drivers, so cached data must have defined validity limits and trigger clear degraded-state warnings when expired.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact time/distance limits must come from operational rules.

Proposed Decision: Loss of connectivity should automatically become visible to Control while the driver also follows the defined communication procedure; neither side relies solely on the other noticing.
Your Reason: SmartRail should detect connectivity loss through connection monitoring and make the disconnected status visible to Central Control. The driver should receive a local warning and follow approved communication procedures. Immediate notification cannot be guaranteed during complete connectivity loss.
Notes / Open Questions: Provides dual detection.

Proposed Decision: Minor-versus-major defect criteria must come from an approved operational/rulebook classification rather than ad-hoc driver or software judgement.
Your Reason: Detailed railway defect classification can remain outside the MVP; staff can report operational incidents through the existing incident workflow.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact criteria remain unresolved.

Proposed Decision: Safety notices should require auditable delivery and acknowledgement, including an appropriate fallback/queued acknowledgement mechanism during outages.
Your Reason: Acknowledgement helps Central Control verify that drivers have seen important safety notices, without adding unnecessary complexity to normal notifications.
Notes / Open Questions: Mechanism must work before shift/journey start.

Proposed Decision: Voice communication should remain an essential degraded-mode/safety channel, not a permanent substitute for normal structured data exchange; significant commands require later audit reconciliation.
Your Reason: Voice communication is an existing railway operational responsibility, so SmartRail should acknowledge it as an external fallback without adding unnecessary implementation complexity.
Notes / Open Questions: Avoid radio/cognitive overload.

Proposed Decision: Define explicit precedence for conflicting journey instructions: approved Control/signaller authority takes precedence over onboard application data, which takes precedence over static documentation, subject to formal railway safety rules.
Your Reason: SmartRail must respect existing railway operating authority and clearly flag conflicting information without making independent train-control decisions.
Notes / Open Questions: Conflicts should be flagged rather than silently overwritten.

Proposed Decision: Defer precision/dynamic braking guides from the MVP; if implemented later, they must remain advisory rather than authoritative train-control functionality.
Your Reason: Dynamic braking guidance is not required by the assessment and introduces unnecessary safety risks and complexity, so it should remain outside the MVP.
Notes / Open Questions: Reduces MVP liability and scope.

Proposed Decision: MVP DMI should receive required authority/clearance through Control rather than creating separate direct modules for shunters, maintenance personnel and other external operational roles.
Your Reason: Specialist railway operations are outside the MVP, and SmartRail should only display authorized operational information without creating new railway clearance authority.
Notes / Open Questions: External systems/legacy workflows may remain outside SmartRail.

Proposed Decision: Train securement/post-journey sign-off should support secure local/offline completion with deferred synchronization rather than requiring cloud connectivity to complete physical securement.
Your Reason: Digital train-securement sign-off is not required for the MVP and introduces unnecessary operational complexity; existing railway procedures remain responsible for physical securement.
Notes / Open Questions: Manual fallback remains required.

Proposed Decision: Only an authorized operational supervisor/control role should be able to release or override a blocked digital post-journey workflow, and the override must be audited.
Your Reason: This override mechanism depends on the deferred post-journey sign-off feature, so it is unnecessary for the current SmartRail MVP.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact authorized role requires organization policy.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail may auto-populate factual telemetry into reports, but the driver should review/edit/confirm relevant data instead of blindly auto-signing generated reports.
Your Reason: Train and journey details are already assigned by operational staff, so automatic population reduces duplicate entry while driver confirmation ensures accurate status updates.
Notes / Open Questions: Protects both efficiency and accountability.

Proposed Decision: Significant verbal operational instructions should eventually be captured as auditable SmartRail events, including deferred synchronization when the data link is unavailable.
Your Reason: Recording verbal instructions is useful for auditing, but existing railway communication procedures remain outside SmartRail, and a separate capture workflow would add unnecessary MVP complexity.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact capture workflow remains open.

Proposed Decision: Use a phased retail model: support direct/agency ticketing only where operators are formally integrated rather than making SmartRail merchant of record for every operator at launch.
Your Reason: Ticket booking is not explicitly required by the assessment, so the MVP should prioritize journey information and avoid complex payment integrations without authorized operator support.
Notes / Open Questions: Avoids assuming universal commercial integration.

Proposed Decision: Non-integrated routes may still be displayed, but they must be explicitly labelled as self-transfer/unprotected where SmartRail cannot guarantee connection protection.
Your Reason: Connection information is useful for passengers, but SmartRail should not guarantee transfers or ticket protection without confirmed operational arrangements.
Notes / Open Questions: Do not present unprotected travel as guaranteed.

Proposed Decision: For tickets sold through SmartRail-supported integrations, SmartRail should provide the customer entry point while actual refund/amendment responsibility follows the applicable issuing/operator commercial agreement.
Your Reason: Ticket refunds and amendments depend on ticket-selling integrations, which are not part of the current MVP; responsibility can be defined when ticketing is introduced.
Notes / Open Questions: Requires contractual rules.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail should only perform settlement/retail integration with operators that have agreed contractual and technical integration; do not assume a universal clearing arrangement.
Your Reason: Multi-operator financial settlement is outside the SmartRail MVP and should only be considered when authorized ticketing integrations and commercial agreements exist.
Notes / Open Questions: Commercial agreements are a dependency.

Proposed Decision: Minimize storage of payment information and use a dedicated/tokenized payment mechanism where direct retail exists rather than storing raw payment credentials inside SmartRail.
Your Reason: Direct ticket payments are outside the current MVP, so payment-tokenization implementation can be deferred while retaining secure payment handling as a future requirement.
Notes / Open Questions: Detailed controls should later be validated by the security review.

Proposed Decision: Journey planning should apply configurable and accessibility-aware transfer buffers, but SmartRail must not claim protected connections unless corresponding operator agreements exist.
Your Reason: Detailed transfer-time calculations are unnecessary for the Sri Lankan SmartRail MVP; passengers can view connecting trains and available alternatives using existing journey information.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact transfer-time rules remain unresolved.

Proposed Decision: Where SmartRail issues/supports digital tickets, use locally verifiable signed/offline ticket credentials, with station/manual fallback available for exceptional device failure.
Your Reason: Offline ticket verification depends on digital ticketing functionality, which is outside the current SmartRail MVP and would introduce unnecessary integration and security complexity.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact barrier technology still depends on implementation scope.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail should detect connection risk and provide alternatives; automatic re-booking/protected status should occur only where operator integration and authority exist.
Your Reason: Providing alternative train information helps passengers continue their journeys during disruptions without introducing unnecessary automation or MVP complexity.
Notes / Open Questions: Otherwise guide passenger to authorized staff/revalidation.

Proposed Decision: MVP should pre-populate known journey information and guide/hand off claims to the responsible operator rather than acting as a multi-operator financial compensation clearinghouse.
Your Reason: Financial compensation claims are not explicitly required by the assessment and would add unnecessary MVP complexity; SmartRail should prioritize disruption information and alternative journeys.
Notes / Open Questions: Consistent with WS-003/WS-009 scope direction.

Proposed Decision: Critical events such as cancellation/platform changes should always generate system notifications; less-critical delay notifications may use sensible system defaults with passenger preference options where appropriate.
Your Reason: Critical journey changes require timely notifications, while configurable delay thresholds prevent unnecessary alerts and keep the notification system practical for the MVP.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact significant-delay threshold remains open.

Proposed Decision: Accessibility information should be detailed and verified enough to support real travel decisions and should include source/freshness information instead of presenting uncertain data as exact.
Your Reason: Basic, verified accessibility information helps passengers plan journeys without introducing complex facility measurements or unnecessary management features.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact measurements/tags need later definition.

Proposed Decision: Physical response to a station accessibility failure should belong to station/operational assistance staff; SmartRail provides detection, escalation, information and status visibility.
Your Reason: Physical accessibility issues belong to station staff; SmartRail should only communicate relevant facility information without introducing complex detection or assistance-management workflows.
Notes / Open Questions: Clarifies digital versus physical responsibility.

Proposed Decision: Unexpected lift/escalator/facility failures should update one authoritative station state and propagate to passenger apps and Customer Service rather than each channel maintaining independent status.
Your Reason: Facility-status consistency is already covered by AD-022 and AD-053; a separate lift/escalator failure workflow would add unnecessary MVP complexity.
Notes / Open Questions: Prediction/coach-position accuracy must be stated transparently.

Proposed Decision: Define the MVP business problem primarily around faster coordinated incident response and accurate real-time passenger communication rather than attempting to solve complete railway-network optimization from day one.
Your Reason: Prioritizing incident coordination and accurate passenger information addresses SmartRail's core operational needs while keeping the MVP achievable and avoiding unnecessary network-optimization complexity.
Notes / Open Questions: KPI framework must measure this baseline.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail incident management should be an active operational lifecycle connected to live journeys/disruptions rather than merely a static incident-record database.
Your Reason: A simple incident lifecycle enables staff to track and resolve railway disruptions while keeping live journey information accurate and passengers informed.
Notes / Open Questions: Strong PO/controller agreement.

Proposed Decision: Passenger CRM, dynamic pricing, automated compensation and similar advanced financial/commercial capabilities should remain post-MVP.
Your Reason: Advanced commercial features are not required by the assessment and would unnecessarily expand the MVP, so development should prioritize core railway operations and passenger information.
Notes / Open Questions: Prevents scope creep.

Proposed Decision: Core journey tracking/state-change data needed for the passenger-information and incident loop should have real integrations from day one; controlled manual workarounds may be accepted only for non-critical feeds.
Your Reason: Reliable internal journey-status integration is essential, but external real-time railway APIs are not guaranteed in Sri Lanka, so authorized manual updates should remain supported.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact critical/non-critical feed classification must be defined.

Proposed Decision: Use strict role-based authorization for safety/operation-sensitive actions, with controller-only operations technically restricted and any exceptional override explicitly audited.
Your Reason: Role-based authorization prevents unauthorized operational changes, while audited overrides provide accountability and protect the integrity of railway operations.
Notes / Open Questions: Avoid purely notification-based authorization for critical actions.

Proposed Decision: Operational truth should originate from authorized operational roles; SmartRail's passenger-information layer should translate/publish that state consistently rather than allowing each channel to independently interpret it.
Your Reason: Authorized operational staff should control official journey updates, while SmartRail publishes consistent information across applications without requiring a separate communications approval workflow.
Notes / Open Questions: Need to decide whether a communications officer approves exceptional messages.

Proposed Decision: Existing safety-critical signalling/interlocking systems remain authoritative for railway movement safety. SmartRail coordinates operational visibility, incidents and communications rather than replacing signalling.
Your Reason: Existing railway signalling systems must remain responsible for train movement safety, while SmartRail focuses on operational information, incident management, and communication.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact integrations depend on available legacy systems.

Proposed Decision: Define measurable latency targets by event criticality instead of using an undefined term such as “real-time.”
Your Reason: Measurable response-time targets help verify that critical railway updates reach users promptly, while allowing practical performance limits for the MVP.
Notes / Open Questions: Precise thresholds remain to be specified.

Proposed Decision: Emergency/multi-agency handovers should be represented explicitly with current authority, handover status, timestamps and acknowledgement rather than relying only on informal communication.
Your Reason: Multi-agency handover management is not required for the SmartRail MVP and would introduce unnecessary operational and legal complexity beyond basic railway incident coordination.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact legal/operational handback process remains organization-specific.

Topic: Network routing vs local platform safety
Proposed Decision: Local physical safety constraints must be capable of blocking/challenging a controller platform decision; conflicts should require an explicit coordinated authorization/handshake rather than silently allowing network optimization to override known danger.
Your Reason: Station safety concerns must be communicated to Central Control, but complex digital approval workflows are unnecessary for the MVP and safety authority must remain with existing railway procedures.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact hierarchy must reflect railway operating rules.

Proposed Decision: Platform changes should use a defined configurable minimum lead-time and local-station acknowledgement where operationally possible; urgent exceptions require explicit override and audit.
Your Reason: Platform changes require timely, consistent communication, but fixed lead-time and additional approval workflows are not defined in the assessment and would unnecessarily complicate the MVP.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact minute threshold should not be invented without railway policy.

Proposed Decision: Emergency services and infrastructure engineers should receive only the minimum role/integration required for their operational tasks; track access and major actions must be recorded.
Your Reason: Direct access for emergency services and external engineers is not required for the MVP; existing railway procedures can handle external coordination without additional user roles or integrations.
Notes / Open Questions: Whether they are direct SmartRail users or external-system users remains to be finalized.

Proposed Decision: SmartRail may detect thresholds and recommend/escalate cancellation, but final operational cancellation should require authorized controller confirmation rather than fully autonomous cancellation.
Your Reason: Train cancellation decisions must remain with authorized railway controllers, while SmartRail handles status updates and passenger communication without unnecessary automated decision-making.
Notes / Open Questions: Avoids assigning commercial/operational authority to automation.

Proposed Decision: Authorized users should be able to override incorrect automated predictions with reason, identity and timestamp captured in the audit trail.
Your Reason: Authorized corrections keep journey information accurate, while audit records ensure accountability without requiring advanced automated prediction systems.
Notes / Open Questions: Formal override procedure remains to be documented.

Proposed Decision: Driver route-competence management should remain an external TOC/HR/competency responsibility; SmartRail may consume a verified eligibility status if required but should not become the training/competency management system.
Your Reason: Driver competency is managed through existing railway procedures, so SmartRail should focus on authorized journey assignments without adding unnecessary HR or training functionality.
Notes / Open Questions: Keeps scope bounded.

Topic: Connectivity failure during live station changes
Proposed Decision: When connectivity fails during a platform change/closure, station staff must retain locally available current information and local safety authority; unsynchronized changes must be clearly marked and reconciled once connectivity returns.
Your Reason: Cached information and pending-update warnings support station operations during outages, while reconciliation prevents conflicting platform information from being silently published.
Notes / Open Questions: Prevent silent disagreement between station and network state.

Proposed Decision: A Station Manager's legitimate local safety veto should take effect immediately for the affected local operation and automatically notify Central Control rather than waiting for network approval before protecting passengers.
Your Reason: Immediate local safety reporting protects passengers, while SmartRail provides central visibility and auditing without introducing independent railway-control authority.
Notes / Open Questions: Must still be auditable and visible centrally.

Proposed Decision: Do not make full automated density optimization a dependency of the MVP. Basic alerts may be used where reliable existing sensors/data are available, while human station context remains authoritative.
Your Reason: Automated crowd-density monitoring is not required for the MVP; existing incident-reporting features can support station overcrowding issues without additional sensors or complex automation.
Notes / Open Questions: Full automated density ingestion can remain post-MVP.

Proposed Decision: Use tiered offline resilience based on station criticality/regulatory needs while preserving essential local capabilities such as safety messaging, cached service information and incident capture.
Your Reason: Basic offline functionality supports Sri Lankan stations during connectivity failures, while station-specific resilience tiers and backup-power requirements would unnecessarily complicate the MVP.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact station tiers and backup-power expectations need definition.

Proposed Decision: Provide station staff with a simple local-status/incident-entry capability for unplanned local failures such as lift, machine or infrastructure outages.
Your Reason: Station staff need a simple way to report local problems, but the existing incident-management system can handle them without additional maintenance-management complexity.
Notes / Open Questions: Should remain lightweight rather than becoming an EAM suite.

Proposed Decision: Use pre-approved announcement templates for common scenarios while allowing appropriately authorized staff to issue exceptional/ad-hoc announcements with audit controls.
Your Reason: Existing station procedures can handle public announcements, while SmartRail provides accurate operational information without introducing unnecessary PA integration or approval workflows.
Notes / Open Questions: Verification/guardrails for dangerous or incorrect messages remain to be specified.

Proposed Decision: Authorized station staff should be able to publish limited local safety/operational messages or override designated display regions without redefining the network-authoritative train-service state.
Your Reason: Local station notices improve passenger safety, while reusing existing information systems avoids complex display overrides and protects authoritative journey information.
Notes / Open Questions: Local versus network display zones require UX/system design.

Proposed Decision: Implement a lightweight report → assigned/in progress → resolved → verified facility-issue lifecycle rather than a full enterprise asset-management system.
Your Reason: Existing incident-management functionality already supports reporting and resolving operational problems; a separate facility maintenance lifecycle would duplicate functionality and unnecessarily expand the MVP.
Notes / Open Questions: Maintenance integration can be expanded later.

Proposed Decision: Support a small, understandable severity/tier model for local incidents so response/escalation differs between minor operational faults and serious safety/security events without introducing a heavy enterprise workflow engine.
Your Reason: A simple severity classification helps operational staff prioritize incidents and communicate urgent safety concerns while reusing the existing incident-management workflow without unnecessary complexity.
Notes / Open Questions: Exact severity definitions require operational validation.

Proposed Decision: Every local station safety override/veto should record the actor, timestamp, reason, affected service/location and resulting state; offline actions must synchronize to the central audit history later.
Your Reason: Basic auditing ensures accountability for station safety actions, while offline synchronization preserves records without introducing a separate safety-override or complex audit-management system.
Notes / Open Questions: Workshop specifically leaves audit requirements open.
